$comment: The design-authority manifest (task 028, corrected by task 030). One current record per governed surface, naming the owner-approved HTML pack that owns that surface's visual anatomy and the SHA-256 of its exact bytes. src/ui/design-authority.test.ts fails when a canonical file, a hash, or a record here drifts. The packs own composition, hierarchy, density, placement, disclosure, table/row treatment, status presentation, interaction and responsive behaviour; they do NOT own product copy (docs/design/content.json) and they do NOT own technical truth (the engine, the baseline, Graph, lifecycle, MFA proof). Packs 031-040 restored the four surfaces onto their packs and task 041 verified them, so every `implementationState` below now reads `restored` and names the pack that did it. `productionAssumedConformant` stays false on purpose and is not a leftover: conformance is EVIDENCED, never assumed. A surface earns it again on every change, by the two-sided anatomy test that reads the canonical bytes at test time (src/ui/surfaces/{connectAnatomy,planAnatomy,readinessAnatomy}.test.ts, src/home.test.ts) and by the rendered comparison scripts/render-design.mjs writes. A commit after this one can regress a surface without touching this file, which is exactly why nothing here may assume. The brand skin is recorded in docs/brand/brand-manifest.json, and the current approved appearance in docs/design/approved/reference/. The four canonical packs live under docs/design/approved/anatomy/ since the design folder was cleaned; their bytes and hashes did not change, only their directory did.
correctionNote: Version 1 recorded each surface under the owner's upload file name (iamai-home-design-pack-v2.html and so on). The canonical repository file names are the short forms below, and task 030 deleted the byte-identical long-named copies so a surface cannot have two current files. The bytes and the hashes did not change; only the paths did. The original upload names are kept as `ownerApprovedSourceName` provenance.

authority.$comment: The three sentences a later pack must be able to read as values rather than infer from prose.

precedence.$comment: Resolution order when two authorities appear to disagree. Truth outranks the picture; the picture outranks the skin. A design that appears to require a different technical meaning does not get one: the design adapts, or the bounded sub-item stops.

observed.$comment: Read directly out of the file by task 030, not paraphrased from a prompt.

surfaces.name: Connect
surfaces.declaredTitleNote: The <title> inside the file still says v1; the owner's file name, and this record, say v3. The bytes and the hash are the identity — a stale title element inside an approved file is not a reason to edit the file.

surfaces.name: Plan
surfaces.sourceNameNote: The (1) is upload provenance from the owner's original file name only. The canonical repository file name drops it; nothing may reintroduce a second current Plan pack under the (1) name.

surfaces.name: MFA Readiness
surfaces.declaredTitle: IAMAI MFA Readiness Design Pack v2

brand.$comment: The approved brand skin. It may repaint the approved anatomy; it may not rearrange it. The machine-readable brand authority is docs/brand/brand-manifest.json (task 029). The current approved appearance is shown by the comparison references in docs/design/approved/reference/, which are derived visual reference and never an anatomy or a copy authority.

generatedPreviews.$comment: Application-page previews produced during the branding exploration. They are brand/colour framing only. This manifest deliberately records no path for them: a generated preview is never an entry in `surfaces`, and nothing may promote one to an application authority. Task 030 re-checked every design and brand record created by tasks 028 and 029 and found no preview recorded as architecture.

renderedEvidence.$comment: Passing code and tests cannot prove visual conformance. A restoration task compares the rendered surface with its pack. The canonical HTML is the authority and a PNG under `output` is derived reference only — never the other way round.
renderedEvidence.walkNote: scripts/walk.mjs renders the built application at 1280 only. Version 1 of this manifest named the walk as the mechanism for all three widths, which was never true; task 030 added the renderer above, which takes all three and renders the canonical HTML itself.

foundation.$comment: What task 030 put underneath the restoration packs. It is capability, not composition: no page anatomy was restored.

layout.$comment: Where the two kinds of design authority live after the design folder was cleaned. They are deliberately not merged: anatomy owns page structure, reference owns the current approved appearance. Production technical/content truth still outranks both.
